MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
November 4, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on
Monday, November 4, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300
Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were
COUNCILMEMBERS: Gazeley, Traina, Savidan, Sanchez, and Mayor Estrada. Also
present were City Manager Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin,
Community Services Director McPherron, Parks and Recreation Director Harding,
Public Works Director Damasse, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the agenda.  Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

3.  PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Estrada presented certificates of recognition to Ron Scanlon, Charles Felix, and
Steve Wolowicz for their continued dedication to, and financial support of the Lomita
Mayor’s Cup Golf Tournament. Mayor Estrada thanked the three men for their hard
work and contributions over the years, which has made the tournament a success, and
noted that those individuals helped start the tournament, with Ron Scanlon continuously
providing financial support. Lastly, Mayor Estrada stated that since its inception, the
tournament has raised over $100,000 for City Recreation Programs including the Junior
Golf program.

  Page 1
 4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Cor Van Diepen, Lomita resident, stated that after routinely flushing his water heater, he
noticed that there are a lot more particles than in the past. According to Mr. Van
Diepen, Lomita has a water issue. Mr. Van Diepen also asked how much the
compensation package was for Fire Captain Lou Currier, who sent out campaign flyers
endorsing two Lomita City Council candidates.

Judy Dailey, Representative of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, invited those in
attendance to the Chamber’s next Business Networking Mixer, which will take place at
Massey’s House of Flowers on Thursday, November 21, 2013, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30
p.m.

Ralph Kallenback, member of the public, asked Council to support House of
Representatives’ Bill No. 129, entitled the “Return to Prudent Banking Act.” According
to Mr. Kallenback, the proposed legislation will rebuild the original limitations that
existed between investment banking and commercial banking, prohibit large banks from
taking speculative actions, and reinstating certain protections of the Glass Steagall Act
that were repealed under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE
  CITY COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina requested a future agenda item to discuss the following: the
sidewalk on Walnut Street, specifically, the west side of the street, north of Lomita
Boulevard; the sidewalk on 256th Street, specifically, on the south side of the street, east
of Walnut Street; and to check traffic on 257th Street, between Walnut Street and
Eshelman Avenue. Councilmember Sanchez agreed to place the proposed discussion
item placed on a future City Council agenda. Councilmembers Gazeley and Savidan
also agreed to placing the discussion item on the future agenda without the discussion
of the traffic on 257th Street.

Councilmember Sanchez announced that another Community Emergency Response
Team (CERT) meeting had been held last week, and that the group is moving forward
with putting together CERT notebooks and updating maps, and will be touring the
Emergency Operations Center (EOC) at Lomita City Hall.

Councilmember Savidan reported that he attended the Halloween festivities at Lomita
Park, the Sister City fundraising event at Alfredo’s, and the Kiwanis Club’s Annual
Pancake Breakfast.

  Page 2
 Councilmember Gazeley stated that he also attended the Kiwanis Club’s Annual
Pancake Breakfast, and that on October 24, 2013, he attended a meeting of the South
Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG), during which issues pertaining to the
MS-4 Storm Water Permit were discussed.

6.  CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that staff was pleased to announce
that after several years of discussion with Los Angeles County over property tax
administration fees, the issue has been resolved, and as a result, the City will receive a
one-time payment of $189,000.

City Manager Rock also stated that starting at 7:15 p.m., on Tuesday, November 5,
2013, staff will begin posting election results on the City’s website.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez requested that Items 7.E and 7.J be pulled for further
discussion.

Item 7.E – Councilmember Sanchez asked whether staff was looking at entities that
would provide and maintain solar panels for City Hall and the Rico Center at no cost, or
for a minimal monthly fee, which Councilmember Sanchez stated would be much less
than what the City currently pays for electricity. Assistant City Manager Sugano
responded that at this point staff is currently evaluating the feasibility of the possible
installation of solar panels at City Hall, and will be starting a similar feasibility study for
Lomita Park. According to Assistant City Manager Sugano, staff will have that
information when the item is brought forward to the City Council for discussion.

Item 7.J - Councilmember Sanchez inquired as to whether staff time will still be involved
if services are contracted out for Community Development Block Grant (CDBG)
projects, to which Community Services Director McPherron responded that a CDBG
related position had been eliminated from this year’s budget and from this point forward
staff  is  recommending  that  a  consultant  perform  the  work.

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve the Consent Agenda.  Councilmember
Traina seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

   b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council meeting

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

8.  Review of the City’s conformance requirements relative to the Los Angeles
  County Metropolitan Transportation Authority’s Congestion Management
  Program (CMP).

  Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that at a prior City Council meeting, staff was
  directed to prepare a future agenda item to further discuss the City’s conformance
  requirements relative to the Congestion Management Program (CMP). According to
  Assistant City Manager Sugano, the purpose of the CMP is to monitor traffic by
  linking local land use decisions with their impacts on the regional transportation
  system. Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that the City is not responsible for
  the implementation of the CMP, but rather it is Los Angeles County Metro that both
  prepares and administers the document. Continuing, Assistant City Manager
  Sugano noted that there had been discussion at the previously mentioned Council
  meeting about the traffic data reports, to which Sugano wanted to clarify that the
  City of Lomita does not have any freeways or intersections identified in the actual
  CMP network, and is therefore not required to provide any specific traffic data to

  Page 4
   Metro. Lastly, in terms of actual conformance with the CMP, Assistant City
  Manager Sugano stated that Chapter 9 of the CMP outlines the guidelines for local
  jurisdictions, which he affirmed that the City has been in conformance with all
  component requirements.

  Councilmember Sanchez stated that Lomita General Plan, which was adopted in
  1988, identified Pacific Coast Highway (PCH), Narbonne Avenue, and Crenshaw
  Boulevard as rated “F” in terms of traffic congestion. Furthermore, Councilmember
  Sanchez went on to say that through the use of the CMP, Los Angeles County
  Metro is trying to make service decisions based on the level of street usage, and
  Councilmember Sanchez inquired as to whether staff had ever requested traffic
  statistics from the Cities of Torrance or Los Angeles in order to get a better idea of
  what the traffic is like at Lomita intersections during peak hours. Assistant City
  Manager Sugano responded that the City does have the most recent annual report
  from CalTrans regarding traffic statistics, and according to Sugano, PCH has been
  identified as having about 50,000 trips per day. Assistant City Manager Sugano
  stated that staff can provide the annual traffic counts along Pacific Coast Highway
  from CalTrans to the Council.

  Councilmember Savidan moved to receive and file the staff report. Councilmember
  Traina seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:40 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
